title: No table, column or request element holds the bids of an auction round
source: Recovery Workbench API Specification v4 schemas AuctionRoundRequest and AssetSale; TSD S5 T3.1; Physical Schema and Logical Data Model v8, listing and asset_sale; legacy RWB-E4-024 Data table
section: s4 Flow; s7 Acceptance criteria; s8 BR5; s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned
description: Legacy RWB-E4-024 lets the vendor report the bids of a round back into the case, but no source names an element that holds a bid, a bidder or a bid count. AuctionRoundRequest publishes roundNo, heldOn, result and price only; the listing object carries round_no and the standard columns only; the service owns two tables, asset_sale and listing, and no bid or round table exists in the physical schema. Where the bids of a round are stored is therefore not specified.
evidence: API Specification v4 /listings/{listingId}/rounds request schema AuctionRoundRequest (roundNo, heldOn, result, price) and response AssetSale; Physical Schema v6 listing columns id, asset_key, sale_channel, start_price, floor_price, round_no, listed_at, status (DF-SAL-001 to DF-SAL-008); Ownership Map S5 tables asset_sale and listing only.
proposed: Record the reported round as the round number, the date, the result and the price of the round, hold the bid list as a gap of this service, and let the DB story or the LDM name the element before a per-bid record is built.

title: No published operation name for the rwb-case state read, the case-move answer, the rwb-payment payment fact or the rwb-partner vendor score
source: Architecture v5 slide 8 and slide 13; Ownership Map; TSD S5 T5.2 and T-A.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-49
section: s3 Preconditions; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes
description: The round branch reads the case state, answers four case moves, asks rwb-payment whether the payment arrived by the due date and asks rwb-partner for the score of a vendor whose award was cancelled. No source publishes the operation names of these rows, and the C row and the I row of this slice in the plan carry none of them.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 13 gives S5 the cells T and E to P8 and S9 and T to P3 without names; the Ownership Map lists no case-move, payment-fact or vendor-score operation; TSD S5 T5.2 says calls go through published interfaces without operation names; the legacy RWB-E4-024 Endpoints table names only POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds and GET /assets.
proposed: Declare the four rows with the placeholder and their gap identifier, build against the documents and their fakes on Day 1, and let P3, P8 and S9 publish the names at the tag of RWB-S5-E4024-CON.

title: Legacy AC2 tests R-DIS-49 while the award and the five-day term belong to FEAT-AST-18, and no source names an owner for R-DIS-49 and R-DIS-50
source: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-47 to R-DIS-50; FSD Epics 3 to 8 v3 module S5 FEAT-AST-15 and FEAT-AST-18; legacy RWB-E4-024 AC2; story rows of RWB-S5-E4024-APP and RWB-S5-E4024-CON
section: s1 Story; s7 Acceptance criteria; s8 Business rules; s19 Out of scope
description: FEAT-AST-18 enforces the five-day payment term (R-DIS-47 starts it and R-DIS-48 confirms the payment), while legacy RWB-E4-024's own AC2 tests R-DIS-49, the cancellation of an award after the term expires, and its Then step reopens the round, which R-DIS-50 implements. The split gives this legacy key FEAT-AST-15 and names no owner for R-DIS-49 or R-DIS-50, so the same rule could be claimed by the payment-term story.
evidence: FSD Epics 3 to 8 v3 feature table rows FEAT-AST-15 (depends on FEAT-AST-14) and FEAT-AST-18 (depends on FEAT-AST-16); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DIS-47 to R-DIS-50; legacy RWB-E4-024 AC2 wording.
proposed: Keep R-DIS-49 and R-DIS-50 with this legacy key because its AC2 tests them, and leave R-DIS-47 and R-DIS-48 with the payment-term story of FEAT-AST-18; record the boundary so the two stories are not built twice.

title: The split plan carries no requirement id for this slice
source: Plan draft of the run; FSD Epics 3 to 8 v3 module S5 FEAT-AST-15
description: The story rows of this slice carry an empty requirement list, so the slice traces to the feature FEAT-AST-15 only, and the header requires the PRD reference to read Pending (C1).
evidence: Story rows of RWB-S5-E4024-APP and RWB-S5-E4024-CON with reqs []; the feature table of FSD Epics 3 to 8 v3 lists FEAT-AST-15 without a requirement id.
proposed: Trace the slice to FEAT-AST-15 of FSD S5 A2.15 and to the epic BRD row for that feature until the PRD allocates requirement ids.

title: The round branch evaluates the DISPOSAL package while DP-04 is outside the pattern set of the slice
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04; story row patterns DP03, DP05, DP13, DP19; FSD S5 FEAT-AST-15; TSD S5 T4
description: R-DIS-36, R-DIS-37, R-DIS-40, R-DIS-49 and R-DIS-50 are evaluated against the DISPOSAL rule package, which DP-04 governs with H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON. The pattern set of this slice names neither, and no source says whether the package load is a capability of the service template or a pattern of this slice.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04 row; the patterns of RWB-S5-E4024-APP and RWB-S5-E4024-CON; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 DISPOSAL rows.
proposed: Load the package in force through the service template, add no H row for the platform rules kit in this slice, and record the reading so the next realignment of the pattern set can confirm it.

title: No element holds the award of a round or its cancellation, while the round write answers a sale record with mandatory dates
source: Recovery Workbench API Specification v4 /listings/{listingId}/rounds response AssetSale; Physical Schema and Logical Data Model v8 asset_sale DF-SAL-012 to DF-SAL-014; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-47 and R-DIS-49
section: s4 Flow; s11 Data; s12.1 REST operations provided; s12.7 Tables owned
description: POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds answers the AssetSale schema, whose contract_date, sale_date and sale_price are mandatory, while a reported round has no contract or sale date yet; and R-DIS-49 cancels an award that the schema carries no award or cancellation element for beyond the standard state column. No source says which element holds a round result, the award it opens, or the cancellation of that award.
evidence: API Specification v4 AssetSale response of API-S5-005; Physical Schema v6 asset_sale mandatory columns contract_date, sale_date, sale_price (DF-SAL-012 to DF-SAL-014) and the standard state column; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-47 and R-DIS-49.
proposed: Record the round on listing and answer the sale record the round opens with its date and price elements completed by the accept and award stories, hold a cancellation in the sale's state element, and keep the placeholder where no element is named.
